enumeration_script.verdict: APPROVE: no input path and no false claim.
verified: No read, no prompt and no human instruction. It prints DLKE_BEGIN, then the inventory JSON with --require-native-keyboard, then either DLKE_SERVICE_PRESENT and DLKE_END, or DLKE_NOT_READY and exit 77.
The DLKE_* markers are disjoint from the interactive DLK_* markers, so no DLK_TYPED or DLK_READY can appear and the interactive claim rule cannot fire.

SERVICE_PRESENT asserts only a registered (kIOServiceMatchedState) PDM1SPIHID, which implies enumeration and IOHIDDevice start completed. The script itself states that this is no proof of native typing or input delivery.
evidence_rule_for_this_mode: Enumeration success = DLKE_SERVICE_PRESENT_<nonce>, plus the IOLog 'PDM1SPIHID: CRC-checked J293 keyboard descriptor acquired (N bytes); input not yet observed', plus the numeric device and interface metadata lines, plus exactly one 'sole probe attempt claimed' and any 'probe refused' lines, plus no 'stopped at' line before DLKE_END.

A 'first device-1 input report accepted by IOHID' line during this unattended run would show that a report was delivered (for example an initial empty report or an accidental touch). It is not typing evidence and must be recorded factually only.

The staged image record must map darwin-keyboard-enumeration a4f64afb to /usr/bin/darwin-keyboard-test and record test_mode enumeration_only. The host TX rule is unchanged (ends with the keyboard command, no other bytes).
